concepts.why: Secular academic / Reformed / Baptist: the name says the water comes from the sanctuary. Ezek 47:1 and 47:12 and Joel 3:18 say so in terms (threshold of the temple; flows from the sanctuary; flow from the house of the LORD). Psalm 46:4 says only that there is a river whose streams delight the city of God, the holy place where the Most High dwells; it does not say the river flows from the sanctuary, so it shares the word river rather than holding the concept. Drop it.

concepts.name: Build the house, so that I may take pleasure in it and be glorified
concepts.why: Secular academic and biblical-theological reader: the name is a question that only Haggai 2:3 asks (and Ezra 3:12 describes the old men weeping). Ezra 3:11, Ezra 6:16, Haggai 1:8 and Haggai 2:4-5 do not ask who remembers the former glory; they tell of laying the foundation, building, dedicating and being strengthened to work. What the passages share is the rebuilding of the house after the exile, so the name should be a text's own words that all six can sit under: Haggai 1:8, quoted exactly. 'Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory?' can stay as the note on Haggai 2:3, which it already is. No passage needs to move.

note_fixes: Matthew 24:2: extend to Matthew 24:1-2, so that the verse that says Jesus left the temple and the disciples pointed out its buildings stands with it; keep the note exactly as it is
Mark 13:2: extend to Mark 13:1-2, so that the temple is named in the text (Mark 13:1 'as Jesus was leaving the temple'); keep the note exactly as it is
Luke 21:6: extend to Luke 21:5-6, so that the temple is named in the text (Luke 21:5 speaks of the temple adorned with beautiful stones); keep the note exactly as it is
concepts.why: Biblical-theological and secular academic reader (does the text say this?): in the packet the three verses never mention the temple. 'These great buildings', 'all these things' and 'what you see here' are the temple only because the verse before says so, and under a Temple theme the text should state it rather than the reader supply it. Jewish reader and Lutheran/Reformed reader: Luke 19:44 is said over the city (the children within your walls) with a charge, 'you did not recognize the time of your visitation'; it shares the phrase 'one stone on another' but is about Jerusalem, not the house, so it does not hold the concept. Dropping it also removes a verse a Jewish reader would take as the site pressing the charge. Dispensational and preterist readers alike can accept the concept once it is only the saying, which it is.

secondary_or_links: Concept 37 (Matt 26:61, Mark 14:58): in the Berean these are the accusers' report of the saying, and Mark and Matthew call the testimony false in the verses just before; the notes quote the report correctly, so no change is demanded, but the drafter should keep the packet's verse text as it is (beginning 'and declared' / 'We heard Him say') so the reader sees these are reports.

Section C and the links: no change. Ten secondary concepts, ten links, every link is a label on the list. No secondary line says one testament fulfils the other; the labels are the texts' own words or plain.
